newsitem.title: CHILE: Allende's eyeglasses to go on show in Chile.
newsitem.headline: Allende's eyeglasses to go on show in Chile.

text.p: The shattered remains of eyeglasses worn by Chile's late Marxist president Salvador Allende during a military coup in 1973 will go on show this week for the first time.

Chile's National Historical Museum will put the socialist leader's trademark thick-rimmed glasses on public view in a glass case starting on Tuesday, said a museum spokeswoman, adding that only the left side, with a shattered lens, had survived.

A Chilean woman found the glasses in the Moneda presidential palace a few days after military jets bombed it in the 1973 coup in which Allende died. She kept the glasses until this year when she donated them to the museum.
Allende's widow Hortensia Bussi and their daughter Isabel Allende confirmed that the glasses were authentic.
